newsitem.title: USA: Minn. hockey boosters eye private arena - paper.
newsitem.headline: Minn. hockey boosters eye private arena - paper.

text.p: The Minnesota group seeking a National Hockey League expansion franchise for St. Paul is considering building a new privately financed arena, the Star Tribune reported Thursday.

The expansion group, one of six finalists for a franchise, is considering a $125 million private facility after plans to renovate the city-owned arena downtown were met with a lukewarm response from the NHL expansion committee earlier this month, the newspaper reported.

The lead investor in the group, Rollerblade and billboard magnate Robert Naegele Jr, is surveying the other members to determine whether they would be interested in a deeper involvement, the newspaper reported.

Plans for the state to provide $51 million of bonds to renovation the Civic Center arena have been advanced in the Minnesota legislature and Gov. Arne Carlson has pledged to spend $5.5 million upfront this year for the facility.
Carlson supports the $51 million bonds whether it goes to renovate the Civic Center or toward a new arena, the newspaper reported.
The Hartford Whalers hockey club has played its last game in Connecticut and groups in St. Paul and Minneapolis are attempting to lure the team to the Twin Cities.
